current: ADR 31/04 prescribes braking system requirements for passenger cars. It applies to MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles (and certain LEP tricycles) from 1 July 2019 and accepts UN Regulation No. 13-H (01 series) as deemed equivalent.
proposed: ADR 31/04 prescribes braking requirements for MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles and certain LEP motor tricycles. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue to comply with ADR 31/03. UN Regulation No. 13-H (01 series) is deemed equivalent.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 31/03. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: ADR 89/00 specifies requirements for Brake Assist Systems on passenger cars and light commercial vehicles to maximise braking performance in emergency conditions. It applies to MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles from 1 July 2019 and deems UN Regulation No. 139 (00 series) equivalent.
proposed: ADR 89/00 requires Brake Assist Systems on MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles to maximise emergency braking performance. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue to comply with ADR 31/03 or ADR 35/05 as applicable. UN Regulation No. 139 (00 series) is deemed equivalent for vehicles equipped with BAS.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 31/03 or ADR 35/05. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: ADR 88/00 specifies requirements for Electronic Stability Control (ESC) systems on passenger cars and light commercial vehicles to reduce the risk of crashes involving loss of directional control, including rollover. It applies to MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles from 1 July 2019 and deems UN Regulation No. 140 and GTR No. 8 equivalent.
proposed: ADR 88/00 requires Electronic Stability Control on MA, MB, MC and NA vehicles to reduce crashes involving loss of directional control. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue under ADR 31/03 or ADR 35/05 as applicable. UN Regulation No. 140 (00 series) and GTR No. 8 are alternative standards, subject to the stated exemptions.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 31/03 or ADR 35/05. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: ADR 94/00 specifies requirements for audible warning devices (horns) fitted to vehicles. It applies to all category L, M and N vehicles from 1 July 2019, and deems UN Regulation No. 28 (00 series) equivalent for categories LC, LD, LE, M and N.
proposed: ADR 94/00 requires audible warning devices on category L, M and N vehicles. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue to comply with ADR 42/04. UN Regulation No. 28 (00 series) is deemed equivalent for categories LC, LD, LE, M and N.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 42/04. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: ADR 90/00 specifies requirements to ensure safe steering under normal operating and failure conditions. It applies from 1 July 2019 to category LB, LD, LE, M and N vehicles, and deems UN Regulation No. 79 (01 to 02 series) equivalent for category M and N vehicles.
proposed: ADR 90/00 specifies steering safety under normal operating and failure conditions for category LB, LD, LE, M and N vehicles. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue to comply with ADR 42/04. UN Regulation No. 79 (01 to 02 series) is deemed equivalent for category M and N vehicles.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 42/04. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: ADR 95/00 specifies requirements for the installation of pneumatic tyres on vehicles. It applies to all vehicle categories from 1 July 2019, and for MA, MB and MC vehicles accepts UN Regulation No. 142 as an alternative.
proposed: ADR 95/00 specifies pneumatic tyre installation requirements for all vehicle categories, excluding temporary-use spare units. It is mandatory for new models from 1 July 2019; other models may continue to comply with ADR 42/04. For MA, MB and MC vehicles, UN Regulation No. 142 is an alternative standard.
evidence: Clause 3.1.1: "1 July 2019 for all new model vehicles." Clause 3.1.2: "There is no mandatory application date for all other vehicles." Those vehicles may continue under ADR 42/04. The current summary states applicability from 1 July 2019 without the new-model limitation.

current: Australian Design Rule 38/05 establishes national standards for trailer brake systems on road vehicles in Australia. It mandates that trailers meet specified braking system requirements as a condition of road vehicle standards compliance under the Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018.
proposed: ADR 38/05 specifies normal and emergency braking requirements for trailers with Gross Trailer Mass exceeding 750 kg, excluding trailers designed for towing vehicles with maximum speed below 50 km/h. It applies to new models from 1 July 2019 and all applicable trailers from 1 November 2019. Compliance may be demonstrated by road tests or calculations using approved component data.
evidence: Clause 3.1: "This standard applies to category T vehicles with a ‘Gross Trailer Mass’ exceeding 750 kg ... (except those trailers designed for use behind a drawing vehicle with a maximum speed less than 50 km/h)." Clauses 3.1.1-3.1.2 specify 1 July 2019 new models / 1 November 2019 all vehicles. Clause 2.2 permits road testing and/or calculations. The current summary claims unqualified applicability to trailers.
